constraints_check.constraint: Tour visits every city exactly once and returns to the start (Hamiltonian cycle).
constraints_check.evidence: assert len(best_route) == n, f"Route length {len(best_route)} != n={n}"; assert len(set(best_route)) == n, "Route has duplicate cities"; assert set(best_route) == set(range(n)), "Route missing some cities" ; route_distance closes the cycle via route[(i + 1) % n]

constraints_check.constraint: Output schema must match evaluator: if benchmark is multi-instance, enumerate every instance and emit one tour per instance.
constraints_check.evidence: multi = group_by_instance(data_file); if multi: for inst, (coords, ids) in multi.items(): tour, dist = solve_one_instance(...); ... w.writerow(["instance_id", "sequence_number", "city_id"]) ...

constraints_check.constraint: Distance computation must be consistent between solver and evaluator (same metric, same rounding).
constraints_check.evidence: DISTANCE_METRIC = "euclidean"  (hardcoded default; no verification against evaluator spec, no support for haversine or precomputed matrices despite the docstring mentioning them)

potential_failures: If the evaluator uses TSPLIB EUC_2D integer rounding, haversine, or a precomputed distance matrix, the solver's reported/optimized distance will diverge from the evaluator's score.
Closure to start: evaluator may require the starting city to be appended explicitly at the end of the tour; the template only relies on implicit closure and notes this without enforcing it.

load_nodes_csv / group_by_instance assume column names from a fixed list ('city_id'/'id'/'node_id', 'x'/'lon', 'y'/'lat'); a benchmark with different column names (e.g., 'X', 'Y', 'index') will silently produce None and crash on float(None).
Output schema column names ('sequence_number', 'city_id', 'instance_id') are assumed; evaluator may expect different headers (e.g., 'order', 'node_id', 'tour_index').

Multi-instance detection relies solely on presence of an 'instance_id' column; benchmarks using a different grouping key (e.g., 'problem_id', 'tsp_id') will be treated as single-instance and produce wrong output.

required_edits.change: Before shipping, confirm the evaluator's metric (euclidean float vs EUC_2D int vs haversine vs precomputed matrix) and set DISTANCE_METRIC accordingly. Add a 'haversine' branch and a 'precomputed' path that loads the evaluator's distance matrix instead of recomputing.
If the evaluator requires explicit closure, append the start city: `id_route = [ids[i] for i in best_route] + [ids[best_route[0]]]` — verify against evaluator spec and toggle accordingly.

Inspect the actual CSV header at runtime; raise a clear error if expected columns are missing. Extend the alias list (e.g., 'X','Y','xcoord','ycoord','index') and allow a config override for column names. Validate that x/y parse to float before appending.
Generalize the instance-grouping key: try 'instance_id', 'problem_id', 'tsp_id', 'instance', 'group_id'. Confirm against the benchmark spec which key applies.
Confirm evaluator's expected header names and order; parameterize header (e.g., 'order'/'sequence_number', 'node_id'/'city_id') to match evaluator exactly.

constraints_check.constraint: Travel time/cost computed with specified speed/service-time model consistently
constraints_check.evidence: route_time_seconds uses trunk_kmh for depot edges and local_kmh otherwise plus service_s per non-depot stop; two_opt invokes the same route_time_seconds function

potential_failures: Template is truncated mid-function after 'CONSTRAINT-CHECK: route starts' — the final assembly of the result, customer-coverage check, and post-split reassignment to vehicle count are missing.
After greedy capacity split, len(final_clusters) may exceed num_vehicles and is hard-truncated by 'final_clusters[:num_vehicles]', dropping customers — violates 'each customer served exactly once'.
nearest_neighbor_route falls back to 'remaining.pop()' without checking edge_feasible, producing a forbidden edge in output (matches Failure Pattern #7: soft fallback emitting infeasible edges).
Closing edge to depot is appended unconditionally even when 'not edge_feasible(cur, 0, ...)'; comment says 'caller should validate' but there is no rejection — forbidden edge can ship to output.

edge_feasible only checks the explicit forbidden set; it does not enumerate restriction types from input data nor mask all cost matrices — risks Patterns #2/#8/#9 if hazmat-style restrictions are present.
two_opt uses route_time_seconds (time) for improvement but no consistency check that the same metric is used in any outer cost aggregation; risk if downstream uses distance.
Cluster merge step ('c.extend(small)') does not recompute or check feasibility of edges between merged customers.
